rationale: MAX of two [0,1] rank gates already tested individually (AccrualBuildWithoutDemand, AccrualBuildDrainingCash) is a mechanical re-blend of the archive's two top signals — the "union vs. intersection" framing is not falsifiable in any economically informative way since MAX of two correlated ranks will track each gate closely and near-certainly reproduce the same alpha.

Industry-standardizing the demand gate is a narrow but genuinely attributive modification of the archive's best signal — it separates firm-specific share loss from shared industry cyclicality — though it is close to the boundary of a cosmetic variant and its upside is limited to confirming that the existing gate's alpha is not an industry-cycle tilt.

Recasting the working-capital stock from an additive leg into the conditioning state for the accrual flow is an economically distinct claim about reversal speed, but the gate RANK(WC/sale) is not industry-adjusted and operating-cycle length is overwhelmingly an industry attribute, so the interaction risks proxying for sector membership rather than firm-level conversion risk.

The financing-source mechanism is genuinely novel, but the gate is internally inconsistent with the accrual leg: Δdlc enters the accrual measure ADD(SUB(wcap,che),dlc) with a positive sign, so RANK(Δdlc/at) is mechanically correlated with the very quantity it is supposed to condition, making the product partly a nonlinear transform of the accrual rather than a clean state variable.

Shortening a window from five to three years and bolting on the archive's ubiquitous IND_ZSCORE gross-profitability anchor is a cosmetic variant of CumulativeProfitAbsorbedByWorkingCapital, and the ratio retains its core defect — a cumulative-gross-profit denominator that can be small or negative, flipping the signal's sign for exactly the distressed firms it targets.

Benchmarking non-cash current asset growth against the cost base rather than sales or assets is the only proposal here introducing a genuinely new denominator with a clear real-earnings-management story, though it sits uncomfortably close to the published Abarbanell–Bushee inventory-versus-sales-growth fundamental signal and to the inventory-growth anomaly, so any result must be shown incremental to those.
